subject: Hosted API streaming chat - critical path: p99 spike during peak & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@glowhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@glowhealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 18:07:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: p99 latency spikes on streaming chat during peak (3/19 evening)

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing severe user impact on GlowHealth's live chat this evening during our 6-8pm PST peak window. P95 is moderately elevated but p99s are spiking to 4-6s for many short conversations using the hosted streaming endpoint (SSE). Some requests are timing out and we're seeing a +12% error rate correlated with the spike. This is causing agents to see delayed replies and users to abandon chat.

We reported an incident earlier to platform@glowhealth.com but wanted to loop you directly because this is affecting our patient-facing flows. Can Redwood confirm scope, root cause, and immediate mitigation? We need a short-term workaround and an ETA for a fix.

Attached: sample curl request IDs and a small trace excerpt.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
Sr. Product Manager, GlowHealth

Attachment: glow-sample-requests.txt (text)

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 18:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: p99 latency spikes on streaming chat during peak (3/19 evening)

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Correlated with 18:00-18:30 PST window; sustained connection churn increased by ~30%.
- p99 token generation latency for SSE connections rose from baseline ~600ms to 3.8s on average; a subset hit 5.6s.
- Error class: increased 502s from the model-serving tier due to transient backend overload and queue timeouts. No TLS anomalies.

Findings so far:
1) A recent autoscaling policy change for a shard serving the hosted streaming routing group reduced burst capacity thresholds (deployed 2028-03-18 02:02 UTC). Under this traffic burst the shard experienced slower spin-up leading to queueing at the request proxy.
2) We observed heavier-than-expected short-session churn from a small set of client IPs (likely real users reconnecting quickly), which amplified queue pressure.

Immediate mitigations applied (18:40):
- Temporarily increased burst capacity and lowered scale-in aggressiveness for the streaming routing group.
- Enabled a soft-degradation route: for requests > 2s we return chunked partial responses faster (config flag) to avoid timeouts and reduce perceived latency.

I've attached sample logs and a short runbook for these steps. Still collecting flamegraphs / further traces. Will update in 20–30 minutes.

Attachments: p99-sample-logs.zip (zip), mitigation-checklist.md (markdown)

— Dev
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec note request: GlowHealth livechat customer impact (p99 spike)

Lauren — cc'ing you for visibility. GlowHealth (regional large customer) saw a p99 spike on streaming chat tonight during peak. Impact: increased user abandonment and agent delays; GlowHealth is asking for an immediate mitigation and an ETA for full recovery.

Short summary for execs:
- Scope: ~18:00-18:45 PST peak window; estimated ~8% of sessions saw >3s p99 latency, ~2% timed out.
- Root cause (initial): mis-tuned autoscaling threshold on streaming shard + concentrated short-session churn.
- Actions taken: increased burst capacity, enabled partial-chunk fallback, collecting traces & logs, rolling transient capacity adjustments.
- Customer ask: short-term workaround and timeline for guaranteed stability during their peak hours.

Proposed asks from leadership: sign-off to keep burst capacity elevated for next 72 hours for this routing group (will incur overage), and approve a small customer goodwill credit if customer requests. Also recommend a post-mortem and autoscaling policy rollback/revision.

I can draft a short customer-facing status note for GlowHealth once I have Dev's confirm that tail metrics are back to baseline.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Technical Account Management, Redwood Inference
